title: Experimental and technoeconomic comparison of honeycomb pad and earthen pot evaporative cooling for photovoltaic panels
content:
Abstract

This study experimentally compares an uncooled photovoltaic (PV) panel with two low-cost evaporative cooling configurations under identical outdoor conditions in Nagpur, India. A system comprises a pump assisted honeycomb-pad evaporative cooling system (PV-HCEC) and a passive earthen pot evaporative water-cooling system (PV-EPEWC). PV-HCEC was tested at water flow rates of 1, 3, and 5 LPM, whereas PV-EPEWC operated through natural thermosyphon circulation. The reference panel reached maximum internal and front surface temperatures of 63 and 68°C, respectively. At 5 LPM, PV-HCEC reduced these temperatures to 49 and 47°C, while PV-EPEWC reduced them to 54 and 52°C. The maximum electrical efficiency increased from 10.71% for the reference panel to 18.06% for PV-HCEC and 16.01% for PV-EPEWC. The maximum thermal and overall efficiencies were 69.65% and 82.89% for PV-HCEC and 62.97% and 75.80% for PV-EPEWC, respectively. PV-HCEC achieved an electricity cost of 5.44 INR kWh−1, an annualized LCOE of 7.06 INR kWh−1, a simple payback period of 6.258 years, an energy payback time of 1.52 years, and net CO2 mitigation of 6.16 t year−1. The results demonstrate that PV-HCEC provides stronger thermal and techno-economic performance, whereas PV-EPEWC offers a simpler pump-free option for decentralized and resource-constrained applications.
